title: Four species again — the conifer you judged was drawing the wrong colours
question: With conifer actually blue-green on rust bark, does the set read as four plants any better than before — or is your "size and colour" verdict unchanged?
context_md:
**A correction, not a retune.** You judged the earlier four-species card and said *"Different-ish. The biggest differences are still size and color."* One of those four was broken when you saw it.

`conifer.ron` shipped with **no `foliage_bands` and no `bark_bands` at all**. My own edit wrote the explanatory note above those two fields and replaced the fields along with it, putting back only the note. Both are `#[serde(default)]`, so absent parses cleanly as `count: 0` — and `count: 0` is the sentinel meaning *"this species never declared a range"*, which makes `banded_shade` fall through to a uniform draw over the **whole** palette. So conifer was wearing a random mix of all eight hues on both axes, in the exact card that was asking you whether the species look different.

It was quietly an economy bug too: the founding leaf-economy allele is derived from the drawn foliage band, so every conifer founded on allele 0 instead of a mixed stand.

Nothing could have caught it — not a parse error, not a panic, not a behaviour any test looked at. A default doing exactly what it promises. There is a guard now (`every_woody_species_declares_a_palette_range_and_they_are_disjoint`), verified to fail both for the missing fields and for an overlap before I kept it.

All four re-rendered on the current head, which also now includes P1's water-book merge, so they are on one engine. Same scene, seed and frame as before. **Only conifer's appearance changed** — the other three had correct bands all along.

I am not claiming this fixes your verdict. The silhouettes are unchanged and your point about the random-walk growth stands. But you judged a set where one member was noise, so it seemed wrong to leave that standing.
